subject: The judgment half of `/skill-fork-sync sync` — steps 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 of skill-fork-sync/references/sync.md. Not an Upstream Fork: the `fork` slot holds this repo's own skill name because the seam derives this file's path from (fork, skill) as evals/<fork>/<skill>.json, so the set stays readable by `--merge-eval-set --fork skill-fork-sync --skill sync-judgment`. How to run it: skill-fork-sync/references/sync.md, section `Self-evals: the gate's own gate`.

run_cost.ceiling_source: orchestrator/docs/adr/0008-diff-targeted-run-budget.md — the same ceiling a sync gets
run_cost.how_counted: the sum of the assertions' `runs` fields. One run per distinct `scenario`: the first assertion of a scenario carries `runs: 1`, every later assertion graded from the same transcript carries `runs: 0`. sync.md step 6 grades every assertion against each transcript, so sharing is the normal shape, not an exception.
run_cost.why_one_run_and_not_two: A fork's skill costs 2 runs — one candidate, one pinned baseline. This set's subject is this repo's own skill, which has no Pinned SHA of itself to compare against, so a scenario is a single run whose transcript is graded against the assertions below.

results_dir: .orchestrator/fork-sync/self-evals/ — gitignored, per RESULTS_DIR in scripts/fork_state.py. No transcript or result file is ever committed.
never_executed: As of issue #7 this set has not been run. Nothing here records an outcome.

assertions.name: holds-a-candidate-that-drops-the-blocked-by-section
assertions.prompt:
You are the judgment half of a `/skill-fork-sync sync`. Build the fixture, read the Sync plan the seam emits for it, then write the report. Launch no worker run of your own.

Fixture, in a scratch directory outside this repo:

1. `upstream/` — a git repo on branch `main` holding `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` = `{"name": "mattpocock-skills", "version": "1.2.0"}` and `skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md`, whose body ends with this issue template, verbatim:

       ## Parent

       A reference to the parent issue on the tracker.

       ## What to build

       The end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work.

       ## Acceptance criteria

       - [ ] Criterion 1

       ## Blocked by

       - A reference to each blocking ticket, or "None — can start immediately".

   Commit it.
2. Clone `upstream/` to `forks/mattpocock/` and add `upstream` as a second remote. That clone's `main` is the Pinned SHA.
3. In `upstream/`, delete the whole `## Blocked by` section from the template and commit. That commit is the Sync candidate.
4. `git -C forks/mattpocock fetch upstream`.

Then, from this repo's root:

    python3 -m scripts.fork_state --evals --clone <abs>/forks/mattpocock --upstream-repo mattpocock/skills --repo .

Now do the judgment half against that plan, per skill-fork-sync/references/sync.md: present the delta before spending anything (step 2), draft the assertions the plan's `referenced_by` files justify (step 5), and write the step-7 report ending in the explicit recommendation.

Draft two table rows: one on the `## Blocked by` guarantee, and one named `requires-an-evidence-section` asserting the template tells a worker what evidence to produce — the template carries no such section at either SHA, so that row fails on both sides.

Grade both sides by reading the two `SKILL.md` bodies out of the fork clone with `git show "${SHA}:skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md"` — brace the variable, because in zsh `$SHA:skills/...` parses as a history modifier and prints the commit diff instead of the file. No worker pair is launched, so the report's Budget section says 0 of 5 runs spent, and — per step 6's rule about evidence that cannot speak to runtime behaviour — the report names its evidence as skill-body content rather than presenting a content check as a behavioural one.
assertions.assert: the recommendation is HOLD, and its reason names the removed `## Blocked by` section plus at least one file in this repo that reads those edges
assertions.check: from the transcript: (1) the `git show` output is the file body, not a commit diff, and has `## Blocked by` in the pinned body and not in the candidate body; (2) the report's last section heading is `### Recommendation: HOLD`; (3) the sentence under it names `## Blocked by` and cites a file the plan lists in `referenced_by` for `to-tickets` — `orchestrator/SKILL.md` or `orchestrator/CONTEXT.md`; (4) the `### Budget` section reads 0 of 5 runs spent and labels the evidence as skill-body content, not runtime behaviour
assertions.why_this_repo_cares: The ready queue is gated on `## Blocked by` edges: `orchestrator/SKILL.md` releases a work item only when every edge in that section is closed, and `orchestrator/CONTEXT.md` defines a work item as carrying them. A `to-tickets` candidate that stops writing the section publishes edgeless items, so the queue releases blocked work and nothing reports that it did. This is the case the gate exists for — an eval set that only ever sees a healthy candidate says nothing about a gate whose value is refusing.
assertions.first_seen_candidate: n/a — drafted for issue #7, not against an Upstream candidate

assertions.name: separates-the-regression-from-a-pre-existing-gap
assertions.prompt: None of its own — graded from the `regressed-to-tickets` transcript, whose assertion table already carries both rows.
assertions.assert: the assertion table marks the `## Blocked by` row REGRESSED and the `requires-an-evidence-section` row `pre-existing gap`, and the reason under the recommendation rests on the REGRESSED row alone
assertions.check: in the same transcript: exactly one row of the `### Assertions — candidate vs pinned` table carries `REGRESSED`; the row that reads fail on both the Pinned and the Candidate column carries `pre-existing gap`; and the string `requires-an-evidence-section` appears nowhere in the paragraph under `### Recommendation:`
assertions.why_this_repo_cares: `sync.md` step 6 makes this the only question a sync answers — did upstream regress — and step 7 holds on a regression on a consumed guarantee, not on a standing gap. A judgment half that cannot tell a fresh loss from a gap that was always there either holds on every sync or holds on none, and either way the gate stops carrying information. The evidence-section row is the control: this repo puts its evidence bar in `docs/agents/orchestrator.md` rather than in the ticket template, so its absence upstream is a gap this repo already works around and is not a reason to refuse a candidate.

assertions.name: reports-no-delta-as-up-to-date-at-zero-runs
assertions.prompt:
You are the judgment half of a `/skill-fork-sync sync`. Launch no worker run.

Fixture, in a scratch directory outside this repo: a git repo `upstream/` on branch `main` with one commit holding `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` = `{"name": "mattpocock-skills", "version": "1.2.0"}` and any `skills/engineering/<name>/SKILL.md`. Clone it to `forks/mattpocock/`, add `upstream` as a second remote and fetch it. Commit nothing further to `upstream/` — the Pinned SHA and the Sync candidate are the same commit.

Then, from this repo's root:

    python3 -m scripts.fork_state --evals --clone <abs>/forks/mattpocock --upstream-repo mattpocock/skills --repo .

Report per skill-fork-sync/references/sync.md step 3 — the short shape, the same sections as the long report with an empty assertion table — and end in the explicit recommendation step 7 requires.
assertions.assert: the report states the fork is up to date, its Budget section reads 0 of 5 runs spent, and no transcript is listed
assertions.check: from the transcript: the plan carries `"up_to_date": true` with `pinned_sha` equal to `candidate_sha`; the report's `## <fork>:` heading shows the same 7-character SHA on both sides of `->`; the `### Assertions — candidate vs pinned` section says there was nothing to assert on; the `### Budget` section reads 0 of 5 runs spent; the `### Transcripts` section says none was launched; and the report ends in a `### Recommendation:` line
assertions.why_this_repo_cares: No delta is the common case — most syncs find upstream unmoved. If the free path is not free, the 5-run ceiling ADR 0008 sets gets spent on the case that had nothing to evaluate; if it is free but silent about it, the maintainer reads a report with no run count attached and cannot tell a cheap sync from a skipped one.

assertions.name: names-both-the-covered-and-the-dropped-skills-in-the-budget
assertions.prompt:
You are the judgment half of a `/skill-fork-sync sync`. Launch no worker run — the subject is the budget accounting, so report the allocation the plan made and say plainly that no pair was launched.

Fixture, in a scratch directory outside this repo. It carries its own consuming repo rather than using this one: the split between Consumed skills and skipped ones is what is under test, and grepping this repo would make the fixture depend on whatever text happens to be committed here.

1. `upstream/` — a git repo on branch `main` with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` = `{"name": "mattpocock-skills", "version": "1.2.0"}` and four skills, each a `SKILL.md` with one line of body: `skills/engineering/code-review/`, `skills/engineering/tdd/`, `skills/engineering/to-tickets/`, `skills/personal/fixture-only-skill/`. Commit.
2. `consumer/` — not a git repo, one file `docs/agents/orchestrator.md` naming `code-review`, `tdd` and `to-tickets` and never naming `fixture-only-skill`.
3. Clone `upstream/` to `forks/mattpocock/` and add `upstream` as a second remote.
4. In `upstream/`, change all four `SKILL.md` bodies and commit. Then `git -C forks/mattpocock fetch upstream`.

Then, from this repo's root:

    python3 -m scripts.fork_state --evals --clone <abs>/forks/mattpocock --upstream-repo mattpocock/skills --repo <abs>/consumer

Write the step-7 report. Three skills are consumed and the ceiling is 5 runs at 2 runs a skill, so the plan covers two and drops one; the fourth is skipped as unreferenced. The Budget section carries both halves, per step 7's first rule.
assertions.assert: the Budget section reads 4 of 5 runs spent, names the two covered skills with their `1 candidate + 1 pinned baseline` split, and `Not covered` lists exactly two entries — the budget-dropped skill and the skipped skill — each with its reason at 0 runs
assertions.check: from the transcript: the `### Budget` section reads 4 of 5 runs spent; it names the same two skills the plan's `budget.spent_on` lists — `code-review` and `tdd`, the first two in path order — each split `1 candidate + 1 pinned baseline`; it calls the 1 remaining run a reserve rather than a quota to fill; and `Not covered` has exactly two lines, one per entry in the plan's `budget.uncovered` — `fixture-only-skill` with `not referenced by this repo` and `to-tickets` with `run budget exhausted (5 runs per sync)` — each ending `(0 runs)`
assertions.why_this_repo_cares: At a 5-run ceiling partial coverage is the normal outcome, not the exception (ADR 0008). A report that names only what it covered reads as full coverage, and a maintainer who promotes on it believes a skill was evaluated when no run ever touched it.
assertions.first_seen_candidate: n/a — drafted for issue #7, not against an Upstream candidate
